content: Darunavir, when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, can reduce the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased toxicity. Co-administration should be avoided during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. Darunavir increases the levels of intranasal metoclopramide by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Concurrent use with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors is not recommended, as the intranasal metoclopramide dose cannot be adjusted. Darunavir significantly increases the levels of oral midazolam and triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the potential for serious or life-threatening events, such as prolonged sedation or respiratory depression. Darunavir increases the levels of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors leads to higher systemic exposure to midazolam, potentially prolonging sedation. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, monitor for increased adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. Darunavir increases the levels of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of nefazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Nevirapine decreases the levels of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir decreases the levels of norgestimate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. Darunavir increases the levels of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. Darunavir increases the levels of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir decrease the levels of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with the Viekira Pak is not recommended. Darunavir increases the levels of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. Darunavir increases the levels of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. Darunavir increases the levels of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. Darunavir increases the levels of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pemigatinib dose. Darunavir increases the levels of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pexidartinib dose. Darunavir increases the levels of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. After discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous pirtobrutinib dose. Darunavir increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. Darunavir increases the levels of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of red yeast rice by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may increase creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis, as red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Ribociclib increases the levels of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin decreases the levels of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases the levels of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rifapentine decreases the levels of darunavir by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir increases the levels of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of riociguat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible. Darunavir increases the levels of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg twice daily if the platelet count is ≥100 x 10^9/L and avoid use if the platelet count is <100 x 10^9/L. Darunavir increases the levels of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous selumetinib dose. Darunavir increases the levels of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir increases the levels of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor is not recommended. Darunavir increases the levels of topical sofpironium by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, as this may increase sofpironium levels and the risk of adverse effects. Darunavir increases the levels of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir and sparsentan may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. Darunavir increases the levels of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases the levels of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust tadalafil dose for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) or erectile dysfunction (ED) as per specific guidelines. Avoid tadalafil when starting cobicistat. Darunavir increases the levels of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite N-desmethyl tamoxifen. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases the levels of teniposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the levels of ticagrelor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Tipranavir increases the levels of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases the levels of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir increases the levels of topotecan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Tovorafenib decreases the levels of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to therapeutic failure. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of efficacy.
